page: Microsoft Azure D2ps_v6 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine powered by ARM64-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors. The configuration features 2 dedicated physical cores addressing 2 vCPUs at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz with one thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration supporting standard AES instructions.

Memory allocation stands at 8.0 GB, delivering 4.0 GB per core to maintain a balanced general-purpose compute-to-memory distribution. The instance is provisioned without bundled local ephemeral disk storage, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent operational filesystems. In addition, the instance contains zero GPU accelerators, focusing exclusively on CPU execution without coprocessors for graphics or deep learning acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the balance and limitations of a dual-core ARM deployment. Single-threaded gzip compression performance is strong, and single-core tasks across Geekbench and stress-ng place in the average tier. However, multi-core compute throughput and memory write bandwidth register lower benchmark tiers due to the constrained physical core count. The underlying ARM architecture provides solid power and qualitative cost efficiency for basic CPU capacity, though parallel processing potential remains restricted.

Microsoft Azure D2ps_v6 is engineered for lightweight cloud workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without large memory footprints. Representative use cases include low-volume web serving, API gateways, microservices, development and test nodes, and scheduled background utility jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ps_v6 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture using Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at 3.4 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators. In synthetic benchmark testing, the platform shows strong single-threaded gzip compression and average single-core computational output, while overall multi-core throughput and memory write bandwidth remain modest due to the two-core footprint. Operating as an efficient, lower-power ARM general-purpose profile, it presents a cost-effective operational profile for resource-constrained environments. Microsoft Azure D2ps_v6 is primarily suited for lightweight web serving, staging platforms, microservices, and modest batch data processing tasks that do not demand extensive parallel compute resources.
